name: Asian Paints Ltd
about: Asian Paints is the largest home decor company in India. The 80+yr old company has major brands like Asian Paints, Apco, etc under its umbrella. The co. is into wall paints, wall coverings, waterproofing, texture painting, wall stickers, mechanized tools, adhesives, modular kitchens, sanitaryware, lightings, soft furnishings, and uPVC windows.

sections.one_liner: India's largest paint/decor company. The key question now: can price rises keep up with 25% input inflation after Sep-26 operating margin (OPM) fell to 15.6%?
business: Paints, waterproofing, adhesives, home décor and lighting. Runs 25 plants serving 60+ countries, with 2.29M KL/yr of decorative paint capacity in India [AR FY26]
Segment shares not disclosed. Standalone FY26 revenue ₹30,680 Cr is 86% of consolidated ₹35,584 Cr. The other ~₹4,904 Cr comes from subsidiaries and international [AR FY26][Numbers]
New products (launched in the last 3 years) are 17% of revenue. Management says industrial will grow faster than decorative [Q1 FY27 call]
Home décor has 74 Beautiful Homes stores, but Kitchen/Bath revenue was declining YoY as of the Nov-25 call [AR FY26][Q2 FY26 call]
financial_snapshot: Sep-26 quarter: revenue ₹9,977 Cr, up 16.9% YoY. EBITDA ₹1,557 Cr, up only 3.6%. OPM 15.6%, the lowest in eight quarters [Numbers]
Trailing 12 months: revenue ₹38,633 Cr, EBITDA ₹7,294 Cr (18.9% margin), PAT ₹4,903 Cr. Sep-26 PAT ₹1,085 Cr, up 6.6% YoY [Numbers]
ROCE 26.3% and ROE 21.8%. ROCE is down from 38% in FY24, so returns have reset lower [Numbers]
Valuation: P/E 45.1x, P/B 10.2x (₹2,324 price vs ₹227 book), dividend yield 1.17%. Price is 22% below the ₹2,986 high and 10% above the ₹2,115 low [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue CAGR is 10.4% over 5 years but 1.0% over 3. FY26 ₹35,584 Cr is only 0.3% above FY24 ₹35,495 Cr: two flat years [Numbers]
FY26 PAT ₹4,395 Cr is still 21% below the FY24 peak of ₹5,558 Cr. PAT CAGR is 1.6% over 3 years and 6.5% over 5 [Numbers]
Annual OPM went 21% (FY24) → 18% → 19%, and ROCE 38% → 26% → 26%. Margins are partly back, returns are not [Numbers]
Revenue YoY swung from -6.1% (Dec-24) to +17.9% and +16.9% (Jun/Sep-26), but Sep-26 EBITDA growth lagged at 3.6% [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings doubled in 18 months: ₹2,290 Cr (Mar-25) → ₹4,596 Cr (Sep-26). Debt-to-equity rose 0.12 → 0.21, still low against ₹21,735 Cr net worth [Numbers]
Standalone borrowings are only ₹1,221 Cr, so ~₹2,700 Cr of FY26 debt sits outside the parent. Its purpose is not disclosed [AR FY26][Numbers]
Cash conversion cycle fell 107 → 84 days in FY26 on lower inventory (142 → 118 days). Restocking at costlier 30-45 day inventory may reverse this [Numbers][Q1 FY27 call]
cash_quality: Operating cash flow (CFO) covers profit: CFO/PAT 1.29x over 3 years and 1.61x in FY26 (₹7,088 Cr vs ₹4,395 Cr) [Numbers]
FY26 free cash flow (FCF) ₹5,604 Cr was 2.2x FY25's ₹2,604 Cr. The jump came mainly from working-capital release (days 52 → 38), not earnings [Numbers]
Implied capex fell ₹2,491 Cr → ₹1,820 Cr → ₹1,484 Cr (FY24-26), with a ₹3,250 Cr VAM-VAE plant committed. FY26 FCF is likely a peak [Numbers][Q2 FY26 call]
narrative_vs_numbers: Agree: the Q1 call's 20.6% consolidated margin matches Jun-26 Numbers (₹2,169 Cr EBITDA on ₹10,542 Cr revenue, ~21%) [Q1 FY27 call][Numbers]
Diverge: management talks of 'margin resilience' despite 25% inflation, but Sep-26 OPM was 15.6%, below the 18-20% band, with EBITDA up only 3.6% [Q1 FY27 call][Numbers]
Diverge: Jan-26 call said volume outgrowing value by 4-5% was structural. In Q1 FY27 value grew 16.6% vs 9% volume, so growth is now price-led [Q3 FY26 call][Q1 FY27 call]
Diverge: standalone EBITDA ₹7,113 Cr beats consolidated ₹6,700 Cr, implying ~₹413 Cr losses elsewhere unless definitions differ. That jars with international strength [AR FY26][Numbers]
guidance: Volume growth 8-10% for FY27, repeated on the Jan, May and Jul-26 calls. Q1 delivered 9%; Q2 volume not disclosed [Q1 FY27 call]
FY27 PBDIT margin 18-20%. H1 consolidated OPM is 18.2%, so H2 must reach at least 18% just to stay inside the band [Q1 FY27 call][Numbers]
Pricing: 10.5-11% in hikes taken by May, but only ~7% realised in Q1. 8-9% expected from Q2, against 25% material inflation [Q4 FY26 call][Q1 FY27 call]
VAM-VAE backward-integration plant, ₹3,250 Cr: Phase 1 from Aug-26, 150,000 MT over 2-2.5 years. The full timeline has slipped from 18-24 months [Q2 FY26][Q4 FY26][Q1 FY27 call]
Industrial should outgrow decorative, but its Q1 margin fell 120 bps YoY because B2B price increases came late [Q1 FY27 call]

bull: Revenue up 17-18% YoY for two quarters with 9% volume: price rises are sticking despite competition management calls 'all-time high' [Numbers][Q1 FY27 call]
CFO/PAT 1.29x, FY26 FCF ₹5,604 Cr and debt-to-equity 0.21: the balance sheet can absorb the ₹3,250 Cr VAM-VAE plant easily [Numbers][Q2 FY26 call]
Backward integration (white cement, VAM-VAE) plus 17% new-product revenue could lift OPM back toward FY24's 21% [Q1 FY27 call][Numbers]
bear: Inputs are up 25% while prices are up 7-9%. Sep-26 OPM of 15.6% shows the gap; H2 likely needs more price rises [Q1 FY27 call][Numbers]
P/E 45.1x on PAT growing 1.6% a year over 3 years, with ROCE down 38% → 26%: the valuation already prices in a recovery [Numbers]
9% volume came off a soft base, possibly boosted by pre-buying before price rises. Urban T1/T2 demand is weak; more hikes risk demand falling [Q1 FY27 call][Q4 FY26 call]
questions: Sep-26 OPM 15.6%: how much was mix versus unrecovered inflation, and when does it recover?
FY26 FCF ₹5,604 Cr, yet borrowings rose ₹1,639 Cr. Where did the cash go?
Why is standalone EBITDA ₹7,113 Cr above consolidated ₹6,700 Cr? Which units lose money?
What further price increase is needed to hold 18% PBDIT margin with 25% inflation?

analyst_pushback.question: How do you define 17% innovation? What margins on new products vs core?
analyst_pushback.response: 3-year launch window. Premium-luxury products support overall margins; not construction chemicals alone.

analyst_pushback.question: Is 9% volume growth sufficient given soft base and preponement from price hikes?
analyst_pushback.response: Acknowledged desire for more. Rural compensated urban weakness; within 8-10% band target.

analyst_pushback.question: When do industrial segment margins normalize? 120 bps drop vs Q1 prior year?
analyst_pushback.response: B2B pricing deferred; key accounts take time. Auto/marine performed well; refinishes slow.

analyst_pushback.question: Can you quantify low-cost inventory benefit and margin impact in Q2?
analyst_pushback.response: Difficult to quantify. Mix of newer 30-45 day inventory at higher cost offsets benefit.

annual_report.business: India's leading paint and décor company offering decorative paints, waterproofing, furnishings, and lighting solutions. Operates 25 manufacturing facilities globally, serving 60+ countries. Revenue FY26: ₹30,680 Crores, EBITDA: ₹7,113 Crores.

segments.name: Decorative Paints
segments.comment: Core business with 2.29M KL/annum installed capacity in India

segments.name: Home Décor & Services
segments.comment: Growing through Nilaya Anthology, 74 Beautiful Homes stores

annual_report.revenue_mix: India-centric operations. Product portfolio: decorative paints, waterproofing, home décor, furnishings, lighting. Channels: B2C retail (Beautiful Homes stores), B2B project sales, influencers.
strategy: Massive brand building and innovation-led product development
Services ignition and décor segment expansion via Beautiful Homes
Regional market penetration and B2B project sales growth
annual_report.outlook: Continue innovation focus and brand strengthening. Expand Beautiful Homes stores and painting services. Accelerate regional markets and institutional B2B sales. Strengthen environmental sustainability credentials.
annual_report.capex_plans: Large capex execution for manufacturing capacity expansion and facility upgrades underway. Specific guidance not disclosed in provided sections.
risks: Shifting consumer preferences toward eco-friendly and comprehensive solutions
Intense competition and market share loss from new entrants
Climate-related physical and transition risks impacting operations
Geopolitical tensions causing supply chain disruptions and material cost inflation
annual_report.flags: Exceptional items: ₹166.5 Cr (FY26), ₹379.6 Cr (FY25). Debt-equity ratio 0.059:1 (up from 0.004:1). Borrowings increased to ₹1,221 Cr. DHS provides external audit without qualifications noted.
